data.narrative:
Orchid is a Series A-stage biotech & health company founded by Noor Siddiqui that has raised $16.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the biotech & health sector, including companies such as Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of the three triangulation methods examined, only stage-progression modeling proved applicable. This method uses Orchid's $16.5M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding an implied valuation of $33M. Peer-median anchoring was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting density thresholds (0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage identified). Public-comp P/S anchoring was inapplicable; while the biotech & health sector median P/S is 6.6x across the three public tickers, Orchid's revenue is not disclosed, preventing ratio application.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $28M to $38M, with a median point of $33M. This range incorporates ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the limited methodological foundation (one applicable method), absence of revenue visibility for private comparables, and the sparse peer set at Orchid's specific stage and valuation tier. A post-Series A financing or revenue disclosure would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
